content_note: Clinic and lab settings used as language contexts. No real drug names, doses or medical guidance appear, and none is intended.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: ब्लड टेस्ट के लिए आना है। कब आऊँ?
lines.read_as: blaḍ ṭesṭ ke lie aanaa hai. kab aauuṁ?
lines.english: I need to come for a blood test. When should I come?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: सुबह आ जाइए, नौ बजे से पहले।
lines.read_as: subah aa jaaie, nau baje se pahle.
lines.english: Come in the morning, before nine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do I need to bring the prescription?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: हाँ, डॉक्टर की पर्ची ज़रूर लाइए।
lines.read_as: haaṁ, ḍôkṭar kii parchii zaruur laaie.
lines.english: Yes, do bring the doctor's slip.

learn.title_en: बजे — the oblique hiding inside every clock time
learn.explanation_en: नौ बजे से पहले, before nine o'clock. बजे is the oblique of बजा, and it is why every clock time in Hindi ends in -बजे rather than -बजा: the time is always sitting in front of something, or at least behaving as though it is. Note also पर्ची लानी होगी? — the obligation ladder with a feminine object, so the infinitive is लानी rather than लाना. That same agreement has now turned up in a cab, a metro station and a pathology lab.
listening_notes: नौ बजे से पहले — से पहले for "before", with बजे already oblique before it.
कब आऊँ? is the subjunctive asking for instruction: when should I come?
डॉक्टर की पर्ची — की because पर्ची is feminine.

practice.question_en: What must the patient bring with him?
practice.explanation_en: Line 4: डॉक्टर की पर्ची ज़रूर लाइए.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: सुबह आ जाइए, नौ बजे से ___ ।
game.question_read_as: subah aa jaaie, nau baje se ___ .
game.explanation_en: से पहले is "before". बाद would need के in front of it, not से.

audio.notes_for_recording: Reception counter, phone ringing behind. Brisk on both sides.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Should I not eat or drink anything?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: बारह घंटे खाली पेट रहिए। और सुबह की दवा छोड़नी पड़ेगी।
lines.read_as: baarah ghanṭe khaalii peṭ rahie. aur subah kii davaa chhoṛnii paṛegii.
lines.english: Fast for twelve hours. And you'll have to skip the morning medicine.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: पानी चल जाएगा। बस और कुछ नहीं।
lines.read_as: paanii chal jaaegaa. bas aur kuchh nahiiṁ.

learn.title_en: छोड़नी पड़ेगी — two words moved by one noun
learn.explanation_en: दवा is feminine, so the infinitive is छोड़नी and पड़ेगा follows it to पड़ेगी. Two words agreeing with a noun that sits in front of both of them, exactly as in Module 11. Now compare the first half of the same line: खाली पेट रहिए has no object at all, so nothing agrees with anything. One sentence, two obligation structures, and the only thing separating them is whether a feminine noun happens to be standing in the way.
listening_notes: खाली पेट — literally "empty stomach", the standard phrase for fasting before a test.
पानी चल जाएगा — चलना for "will do, is acceptable", the same idiom as सफ़ेद भी चलेगा in the clothes shop.
खाना-पीना as a paired noun means food and drink in general. Hindi pairs verbs like this constantly: आना-जाना, लेना-देना.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: और सुबह की दवा छोड़नी ___ ।
game.explanation_en: दवा is feminine singular, so the infinitive is छोड़नी and the modal follows it.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 2 is delivered as a routine. Line 3 is genuinely worried.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: I've come to collect a report.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: नाम बताइए। कब टेस्ट करवाया था?
lines.read_as: naam bataaie. kab ṭesṭ karvaayaa thaa?
lines.english: Name? When did you get the test done?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: हाँ, तैयार है। आपने पैसे जमा किए थे?
lines.read_as: haaṁ, taiyaar hai. aapne paise jamaa kie the?
lines.english: Yes, it's ready. Did you pay?

learn.title_en: लेने आया हूँ — the infinitive of purpose
learn.explanation_en: रिपोर्ट लेने आया हूँ is "I've come to collect a report". The infinitive goes oblique — लेने, not लेना — when it states the purpose of coming or going. You will hear this constantly: खाने आया हूँ, मिलने गया था, पूछने आई हूँ. There is no separate word for "in order to" anywhere in the sentence; the oblique ending is doing the whole job on its own.
listening_notes: आपने पैसे जमा किए थे? — जमा करना is transitive, so ने, and किए agrees with masculine plural पैसे.
परसों means both the day before yesterday and the day after tomorrow. Context decides, and here the past tense settles it.
उसी दिन — उस plus ही, "that very day".

options: The day before yesterday, in the morning

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: हाँ, तैयार है। ___ पैसे जमा किए थे?
game.question_read_as: haaṁ, taiyaar hai. ___ paise jamaa kie the?
game.explanation_en: जमा करना is transitive and the tense is perfective, so ने.

audio.notes_for_recording: Counter noise. Line 4 is asked while looking at a screen.

summary.recap_en: Clock times are always oblique — नौ बजे — because they behave as though a postposition follows. An obligation with a feminine object moves two words: दवा छोड़नी पड़ेगी. And the oblique infinitive states purpose all by itself: रिपोर्ट लेने आया हूँ.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the dentist, and the difficulty of naming a tooth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: दाँत में बहुत दर्द है। आज दिखा सकते हैं?
lines.read_as: daaṁt meṁ bahut dard hai. aaj dikhaa sakte haiṁ?
lines.english: My tooth's hurting a lot. Can you see me today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: आज तो फ़ुल है। अगले हफ़्ते का दे दूँ?
lines.read_as: aaj to ful hai. agle hafte kaa de duuṁ?
lines.english: Today's full. Shall I give you next week?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: रुकिए, शाम को एक स्लॉट खाली हुआ है।
lines.read_as: rukie, shaam ko ek slôṭ khaalii huaa hai.
lines.english: Hold on — a slot's opened up this evening.

learn.title_en: अगले हफ़्ते का — an oblique before an invisible noun
learn.explanation_en: अगले हफ़्ते का दे दूँ? — "shall I give you next week's?" There is no noun after का at all; स्लॉट is understood and never said. हफ़्ता still goes oblique to हफ़्ते because का follows it, and अगला follows to अगले. Hindi drops the noun and keeps every ending that was pointing at it, which is why in fast speech the agreements are often the only thing left telling you what is under discussion.
listening_notes: दिखा सकते हैं? — दिखाना, the causative of देखना, plus सकना. Literally "can you show", meaning "can you see me".
कर पाऊँगा — पाना from Module 11 in the future: I won't manage to.
आज तो फ़ुल है — तो marking contrast, and फ़ुल used as an ordinary Hindi adjective.

practice.question_en: When does he end up getting an appointment?
practice.explanation_en: Line 4: शाम को एक स्लॉट खाली हुआ है.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: आज तो फ़ुल है। अगले ___ का दे दूँ?
game.question_read_as: aaj to ful hai. agle ___ kaa de duuṁ?
game.explanation_en: का is a postposition, so हफ़्ता goes oblique to हफ़्ते.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 3 is genuinely in pain. Line 4 comes after a pause and a keyboard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: नीचे वाला। मसूड़े के नीचे भी दर्द है।
lines.read_as: niiche vaalaa. masuuṛe ke niiche bhii dard hai.
lines.english: The lower one. It hurts under the gum too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: All right, we'll need an X-ray.

learn.title_en: वाला pointing at things you can both see
learn.explanation_en: ये वाला, ऊपर वाला, नीचे वाला — वाला is doing the same job it did with रोज़ वाली चाय and गार्ड वाले गेट, but here it is pointing at physical things in front of both speakers. It agrees with what it stands for, so वाला for masculine दाँत. When a dentist asks कौन सा, the answer will almost always be a वाला phrase, because pointing is easier than naming a tooth in any language.
listening_notes: मसूड़े के नीचे — मसूड़ा goes oblique to मसूड़े before के नीचे.
पीछे की तरफ़ — की because तरफ़ is feminine. Direction words in Hindi mostly are.
करवाना पड़ेगा — the second causative plus the obligation ladder: we'll have to have one done.

options: An upper one at the back
An upper one at the front
A lower one towards the back
practice.explanation_en: Lines 2 and 4: पीछे की तरफ़, and नीचे वाला.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: मसूड़े के ___ भी दर्द है।
game.explanation_en: के नीचे is under. के ऊपर would be above it.

audio.notes_for_recording: The patient's lines are slightly muffled — he is being examined while speaking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: रूट कैनाल है, तो पाँच-छह हज़ार लगेंगे।
lines.read_as: ruuṭ kainaal hai, to paaṁch-chhah hazaar lageṁge.
lines.english: It's a root canal, so five or six thousand.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: एक ही बार में हो जाएगा?
lines.read_as: ek hii baar meṁ ho jaaegaa?
lines.english: Will it be done in one go?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, it'll take two or three sittings.

learn.title_en: लगेंगे and लगेंगी, two lines apart
learn.explanation_en: पाँच-छह हज़ार लगेंगे in line 2, and दो-तीन सिटिंग लगेंगी in line 4. Same verb, same construction, and the endings differ because हज़ार is masculine and सिटिंग is feminine. English loanwords ending in -ing come into Hindi as feminine — मीटिंग, सिटिंग, बुकिंग, पार्किंग — which is worth knowing because they turn up constantly in any professional setting and they all behave the same way.
listening_notes: खर्चा आएगा — an expense "comes" rather than "is". लगेगा would work here too.
एक ही बार में — ही narrowing it to one single go.
हफ़्ते-हफ़्ते भर का — the doubled word again, meaning roughly "a week or so each time".

practice.question_en: How many appointments will it take?

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: नहीं, दो-तीन सिटिंग ___ ।
game.explanation_en: सिटिंग is feminine and plural here, so लगेंगी — against masculine हज़ार लगेंगे two lines earlier.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 1 is apprehensive. The dentist is matter-of-fact throughout.

summary.recap_en: वाला lets you point instead of naming, which is how anyone identifies a tooth. Hindi drops the noun and keeps its agreements — अगले हफ़्ते का, with स्लॉट never said. And English -ing loanwords are feminine: सिटिंग लगेंगी against हज़ार लगेंगे.
summary.next_up_en: Next: getting better, and being told not to rush it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: पहले से बेहतर है। बुख़ार नहीं आया।
lines.read_as: pahle se behtar hai. buḳhaar nahiiṁ aayaa.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: थोड़ी है, पर बहुत कम हो गई है।
lines.read_as: thoṛii hai, par bahut kam ho gaii hai.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: अच्छा है। दवा पूरी कर लीजिए।
lines.read_as: acchaa hai. davaa puurii kar liijie.

learn.title_en: पहले से बेहतर — comparing against a time
learn.explanation_en: पहले से बेहतर, better than before. से for comparison again, and this time what is being compared against is not a thing but an earlier moment. That is worth noticing, because English changes word here — "than before" rather than "than X" — and Hindi changes nothing at all. Note also दवा पूरी कर लीजिए, finish the medicine, where पूरी is feminine because दवा is, and the लेना vector adds that it is for the patient's own good.
listening_notes: कमज़ोरी बहुत कम हो गई है: कमज़ोरी is feminine, so गई.
बुख़ार नहीं आया — a fever "comes" in Hindi, so its absence is that it did not come.
अब कैसा लग रहा है? — लगना for how something seems, from Module 10, with the dative dropped as usual.

practice.question_en: What does the doctor tell him at the end?

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: थोड़ी है, पर बहुत कम हो ___ है।
game.question_read_as: thoṛii hai, par bahut kam ho ___ hai.
game.explanation_en: कमज़ोरी is feminine, so the vector is गई.

audio.notes_for_recording: Both noticeably lighter in tone than the first consultation.

items.title_en: A friend asks how you are

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: ठीक हूँ यार। कमज़ोरी बस थकान से है।
lines.read_as: ṭhiik huuṁ yaar. kamzorii bas thakaan se hai.
lines.english: I'm fine. The weakness is just from tiredness.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: हाँ, दो दिन छुट्टी ली थी।
lines.read_as: haaṁ, do din chhuṭṭii lii thii.
lines.english: Yes, I took two days off.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: अच्छा किया। जल्दी काम पर मत लौटना।
lines.read_as: acchaa kiyaa. jaldii kaam par mat lauṭnaa.
lines.english: Good. Don't go back to work too soon.

learn.explanation_en: कमज़ोरी थकान से है — the weakness is from tiredness. This is the same cause-marking से as किसी दवा से एलर्जी in level 20, and it is one of से's most useful jobs, because Hindi reaches for it wherever English would say "because of", "from" or "due to". Note also मत लौटना in line 5 — मत for an instruction, and the plain infinitive as a gentle command. Together they make it advice between friends rather than an order.
listening_notes: आराम कर रहे हो ना? — the ना tag from level 15, expecting agreement rather than information.
अच्छा किया — "you did well". Strictly तुमने अच्छा किया; the subject drops because it is obvious.
काम पर लौटना — work takes पर, not में or को.

practice.question_en: What does the friend advise at the end?
options: Don't go back to work too soon
practice.explanation_en: Line 5: जल्दी काम पर मत लौटना.

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: कमज़ोरी बस थकान ___ है।
game.explanation_en: से marks the cause — the weakness comes from the tiredness.

audio.notes_for_recording: Informal, warm. Line 5 is affectionate scolding.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: कहा कि तीन दिन आराम करो।
lines.read_as: kahaa ki tiin din aaraam karo.
lines.english: He said rest for three days.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: वो पूरी करनी है। बीच में छोड़ी तो फिर से शुरू।
lines.read_as: vo puurii karnii hai. biich meṁ chhoṛii to phir se shuruu.
lines.english: I have to finish it. Stop halfway and you start again.

learn.explanation_en: डॉक्टर ने कहा कि तीन दिन आराम करो. कि introduces reported speech, and Hindi does not shift the tense or the person the way English does — the doctor's actual words come through almost intact, imperative and all. English would say "he said to rest for three days" and rebuild the whole clause; Hindi keeps करो. Once you stop waiting for a transformation that never arrives, reported speech becomes one of the easier things to follow at speed.
listening_notes: सही कहा उन्होंने — the ने-subject at the very end again, emphatic and entirely normal.
वो पूरी करनी है — दवा is feminine, so both पूरी and करनी. The obligation ladder once more.
बीच में छोड़ी तो फिर से शुरू — no verb at all in the second half. Conditionals compress hard in speech.

practice.question_en: How long was he told to rest?

game.question_en: Listen again. Which form fills the gap?
game.question: डॉक्टर ___ क्या कहा?
game.explanation_en: कहना is transitive and the tense is perfective, so the noun subject takes a separate ने.

audio.notes_for_recording: Line 4 is recited — he is repeating what he was told. Line 5 is approving.

summary.recap_en: से compares against a time as easily as against a thing — पहले से बेहतर — and marks cause: थकान से. मत plus a plain infinitive is advice rather than an order. And reported speech with कि keeps the original words intact instead of rebuilding them.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the telephone — asking for someone, wrong numbers, and a bad line.
